items.description: Analyze repository structure and available tooling
items.acceptance_criteria: Document in results/phase1/repo_analysis.md listing: (1) all modules (.archivara/, .opencode/, tools), (2) agent roles and permissions from opencode.json, (3) concept_evolve commands and their outputs, (4) semantic_scholar capabilities. File must be >=50 lines.

items.description: Conduct comprehensive web-based literature review on univalent Bloch constant and related constants
items.acceptance_criteria: Use websearch and webfetch to find and summarize at least 15 papers on: (a) Bloch constant B, (b) locally univalent Bloch constant B_l, (c) Landau constant L, (d) univalent Bloch constant B_u, (e) extremal domain constructions, (f) computational approaches. Create results/phase1/literature_review.md with structured summaries of each paper including authors, year, key results, and methods used.

items.description: Build and maintain sources.bib with BibTeX entries for all consulted references
items.acceptance_criteria: sources.bib in repo root contains valid BibTeX entries for at least 15 relevant papers including: Bhowmik-Sen 2023, Skinner 2009, Yanagihara 1995, Carroll-Ortega-Cerda 2009, Bonk 1990, Bonk-Minda-Yanagihara 1996, Chen-Gauthier 1996, Xiong 2004, Baernstein-Vinson 1995, Rettinger 2008/2012, Ahlfors-Grunsky 1937, Robinson 1935, Goodman 1935/1945, Rademacher 1943, Minda 1990. Each entry must have author, title, journal, year, and doi/url fields.

items.description: Formalize the mathematical problem and chain of inequalities B <= B_l <= L <= B_u
items.acceptance_criteria: Create results/phase1/problem_formalization.md containing: (1) rigorous definitions of B, B_l, L, B_u with LaTeX, (2) proofs or references for each inequality in the chain, (3) table of all known bounds (lower and upper) for each constant with citations, (4) identification of which bound improvements would cascade to B_u. File must be >=80 lines.

items.description: Analyze Skinner's 2009 method for the current best lower bound B_u > 0.5708858
items.acceptance_criteria: Create results/phase1/skinner_analysis.md with: (1) description of Skinner's implicit function technique, (2) how the bootstrap from B(|z|) to C(|z|) works, (3) identification of specific steps where tighter intermediate estimates could improve the final bound, (4) at least 3 concrete ideas for potential improvement. File must be >=60 lines.

items.description: Run ConceptEvolve to explore cross-domain approaches for tightening Bloch constant bounds
items.acceptance_criteria: Execute concept_evolve evolve with topic 'tighter bounds on univalent Bloch constant B_u via extremal domain analysis, conformal mapping optimization, and computational function theory'. Verify results/concept_evolve/tree/ contains at least 7 concept folders each with concept.json and README.md. Verify steering_directions.json has at least 3 directions.
items.notes: Subagent delegation: concept-tree-explorer agent should analyze the resulting tree for high-value paths.

items.description: Implement computational verification of the known lower bound B_u > 0.5708858
items.acceptance_criteria: Create results/phase2/baseline_verification.py (or .sage) that: (1) implements the Koebe function distortion estimates, (2) computes B_f for a family of test univalent functions (Koebe, rotations, convex combinations), (3) numerically verifies that B_f >= 0.5708858 for all tested functions, (4) outputs results to results/phase2/baseline_results.json with at least 10 test cases. Script must run without errors.

items.description: Implement the Bonk-Minda distortion framework for locally univalent Bloch functions
items.acceptance_criteria: Create results/phase2/distortion_framework.py implementing: (1) the Schwarz-Pick derivative bound, (2) the distortion theorem from Bonk-Minda-Yanagihara 1996, (3) area estimates via subordination, (4) numerical evaluation of the distortion bounds. Include unit tests that verify the framework reproduces known bounds from the literature. Output comparison table in results/phase2/distortion_comparison.md.

items.description: Implement Carroll-Ortega-Cerda upper bound construction for B_u
items.acceptance_criteria: Create results/phase2/upper_bound_construction.py that: (1) constructs the modified Goodman domain with harmonic symmetry, (2) numerically computes B_u <= 0.6564 via the Polya-Chebotarev problem for 4 symmetric points, (3) visualizes the extremal domain in figures/upper_bound_domain.png. Results documented in results/phase2/upper_bound_analysis.md with comparison to trivial bound B_u <= 1.

items.description: Establish computational metric framework for measuring bound improvements
items.acceptance_criteria: Create results/phase2/metrics.json defining: (1) primary metric = new_lower_bound - 0.5708858 (improvement over Skinner), (2) secondary metric = 0.6564 - new_lower_bound (gap to best upper bound), (3) tertiary metric = number of digits of precision in the bound. Create results/phase2/metrics_framework.py that computes these metrics from candidate bounds and logs them. All metric values must be computable and reproducible.

items.description: Use literature-graph-miner subagent to mine citation graph for transferable techniques
items.acceptance_criteria: Delegate to literature-graph-miner agent: starting from Skinner 2009, Carroll-Ortega-Cerda 2009, and Bonk-Minda-Yanagihara 1996, build a 2-hop citation graph. Identify at least 5 papers not already in sources.bib that use techniques potentially transferable to the B_u problem. Add new papers to sources.bib. Summarize findings in results/phase2/citation_mining.md.

items.description: Develop improved lower bound via refined Skinner bootstrap with tighter intermediate estimates
items.acceptance_criteria: Create results/phase3/refined_bootstrap.py that: (1) replaces Skinner's original B(|z|) with a tighter initial estimate derived from updated Koebe-type distortion, (2) iterates the implicit function technique with finer step sizes, (3) produces a candidate lower bound > 0.5708858. Document the mathematical derivation in results/phase3/refined_bootstrap_proof.md with full details. The candidate bound must be stated with at least 7 decimal places.

items.description: Investigate extremal domain approach: optimize the shape of simply connected domains to reduce B_f
items.acceptance_criteria: Create results/phase3/extremal_domain_search.py that: (1) parameterizes simply connected domains D with f'(0)=1 (e.g., via slit mappings or conformal map coefficients), (2) uses numerical optimization (gradient descent or genetic algorithm) to minimize B_f over the parameter space, (3) identifies the extremal domain achieving the smallest B_f, (4) outputs the extremal B_f value and domain description in results/phase3/extremal_domain_results.json. The search must cover at least 1000 candidate domains.

items.description: Analyze harmonic symmetry approach: extend Carroll-Ortega-Cerda construction for tighter upper bound on B_u
items.acceptance_criteria: Create results/phase3/harmonic_symmetry.py that: (1) implements the conformal welding technique for domains with n-fold symmetry (n=3,4,5,6), (2) computes B_u upper bounds for each symmetry order, (3) determines whether higher symmetry orders yield tighter bounds than the 3-fold case. Results in results/phase3/harmonic_symmetry_results.md comparing all cases with the Carroll-Ortega-Cerda bound ~0.6564.

items.description: Develop novel approach: area-based lower bound via integral means spectrum
items.acceptance_criteria: Create results/phase3/area_method.py that: (1) implements Gronwall area theorem estimates for univalent functions, (2) uses the integral means spectrum beta(p) to derive area-based lower bounds on B_f, (3) combines with coefficient estimates (de Branges theorem/Bieberbach) to obtain a lower bound on B_u. Document the mathematical argument in results/phase3/area_method_derivation.md. The candidate bound must be explicitly computed and compared to 0.5708858.

items.description: Run ConceptEvolve probe on the specific bottleneck of the Skinner implicit function saturation
items.acceptance_criteria: Execute concept_evolve probe with problem 'Why does Skinner\'s implicit function bootstrap for B_u saturate at 0.5708858? What mathematical barriers prevent further iteration? Can cross-domain optimization techniques break through this saturation?'. Verify results/concept_evolve/probe_result.json exists with at least 3 steering directions. Synthesize key insights in results/phase3/bottleneck_analysis.md.
items.notes: Subagent delegation: concept-tree-explorer agent should walk the concept tree to identify novel attack vectors.

items.description: Investigate Rettinger-style computational approach: algorithmic approximation of B_u from both sides
items.acceptance_criteria: Create results/phase3/computational_bounds.py that: (1) implements a systematic search over univalent functions to compute B_f for a large family (polynomials up to degree N, truncated power series), (2) tracks the infimum of B_f values as N increases, (3) provides a rigorous or near-rigorous lower bound by validated numerics. Output convergence data to results/phase3/computational_convergence.json with at least 20 data points. Compare asymptotic trend to 0.5708858.

items.description: Validate all candidate bounds against known results and cross-check with independent methods
items.acceptance_criteria: Create results/phase4/validation.md that: (1) for each candidate bound from Phase 3, provides an independent numerical verification, (2) cross-checks the refined bootstrap bound against the area method bound, (3) verifies consistency with the chain B <= B_l <= L <= B_u, (4) confirms no candidate lower bound exceeds the Carroll-Ortega-Cerda upper bound ~0.6564. All checks must pass.

items.description: Compare new bounds against all prior work from literature review
items.acceptance_criteria: Create results/phase4/comparison_table.md with a comprehensive table comparing: (1) new lower bound vs. Skinner 0.5708858, (2) new lower bound vs. Yanagihara 0.5 + 10^{-335}, (3) improvement delta with at least 7 significant digits, (4) comparison of methods used (bootstrap, area, extremal domain). Table must reference sources.bib entries. Include a timeline figure in figures/bounds_timeline.png showing historical progression of bounds.

items.description: Conduct sensitivity analysis on the parameters of the most promising approach
items.acceptance_criteria: Create results/phase4/sensitivity_analysis.py that: (1) identifies the most promising bound-improvement approach from Phase 3, (2) varies key parameters (step size, truncation order, number of iterations) by +/- 20%, (3) measures how the final bound changes with each parameter perturbation, (4) identifies which parameter most sensitively affects the bound. Output results to results/phase4/sensitivity_results.json and visualize in figures/sensitivity.png.

items.description: Attempt rigorous proof sketch for any improvement beyond 0.5708858
items.acceptance_criteria: Create results/phase4/proof_sketch.md that: (1) states the main theorem (B_u > X for the new bound X), (2) outlines the proof in at most 10 clearly numbered steps, (3) identifies which steps are fully rigorous vs. relying on numerical computation, (4) explicitly states any unproven assumptions. If no improvement beyond 0.5708858 is achieved, document the barriers encountered and the closest approach. File must be >= 80 lines.

items.description: Use concept-tree-explorer subagent to synthesize findings across all concept folders
items.acceptance_criteria: Delegate to concept-tree-explorer agent: walk the concept tree in results/concept_evolve/tree/ with depth 4, identify the top 3 highest-value concept paths for improving B_u bounds, and propose which paths merit further investigation. Write synthesis to results/phase4/concept_synthesis.md with specific recommendations for each path.

items.description: Write comprehensive research report summarizing all findings
items.acceptance_criteria: Create results/phase5/research_report.md (>= 200 lines) containing: (1) Abstract summarizing the main result, (2) Introduction with problem context and relation to prior work (citing >= 10 entries from sources.bib), (3) Methods section describing each approach attempted, (4) Results section with the best achieved bounds (both lower and upper), (5) Discussion comparing to Skinner 2009 and Carroll-Ortega-Cerda 2009, (6) Conclusion with open questions. All claims must be supported by references or computational evidence from earlier phases.

items.description: Create structured summary of new bounds achieved
items.acceptance_criteria: Create results/phase5/new_bounds_summary.json containing: (1) best_lower_bound (numeric), (2) best_upper_bound (numeric), (3) improvement_over_skinner (numeric or null), (4) method_used (string), (5) confidence_level (one of: 'rigorous', 'numerical', 'heuristic'), (6) open_problems (array of strings). JSON must be valid and all numeric values must have at least 7 decimal places.

items.description: Ensure reproducibility: document all computational steps and dependencies
items.acceptance_criteria: Create results/phase5/reproducibility.md containing: (1) list of all Python/Sage scripts with their purposes, (2) required packages and versions, (3) step-by-step instructions to reproduce all computational results, (4) expected runtime for each script, (5) checksums or expected outputs for validation. A reviewer following these instructions should be able to reproduce all numerical results from Phase 3 and 4.

items.description: Compile LaTeX research paper with formal presentation of results
items.acceptance_criteria: Create research_paper.tex in repo root that: (1) follows standard math journal format (amsart or similar), (2) includes abstract, introduction, preliminaries, main results, proofs/computations, discussion, references, (3) uses BibTeX with sources.bib, (4) includes at least 2 figures from figures/, (5) states any new bounds as formal theorems or propositions. Paper must compile (or be compilable) to PDF.

items.description: Conduct final review and identify future research directions using literature-graph-miner
items.acceptance_criteria: Delegate to literature-graph-miner agent: using the final results, search for very recent papers (2024-2026) on Bloch constants, extremal problems for univalent functions, and computational function theory. Identify at least 3 future research directions that could further improve B_u bounds. Write results/phase5/future_directions.md with specific actionable proposals, each referencing at least one paper from sources.bib.
items.notes: Subagent delegation: literature-graph-miner agent for final synthesis.
